cohort: This study included 501 women who completed questionnaires during pre-pregnancy, early, mid, and late pregnancy, and at five time points during the first year postpartum.
finding: Gestational week and previous vaginal deliveries increased the risk of cumulative incidence of urinary incontinence during pregnancy, while full-time employment, higher BMI, vaginal delivery, and UI during early and mid-pregnancy increased the risk during the first year postpartum.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery increased the risk of cumulative incidence of urinary incontinence during the first year postpartum.
